stem_book: Figure shows an enemy tank moving with a speed of 9 m/s in the direction shown in figure (at 37° to the 360 m perpendicular, towards the plane of firing). A gun at the origin can fire shells in the y-z plane only, with a speed 100 m/s at an angle of 53° with the horizontal. Tank is initially at a perpendicular distance of 360 m from the plane of firing, and its path meets that plane at the point where the shell lands. If the tank started at t = 0, then after what time interval (in s) is the shell to be fired to hit the tank? (g = 10 m s⁻²)
reason: Stem made explicit that the tank's path crosses the firing plane at the shell's landing point (implied by figure, needed for a unique answer); g = 10 added.
work: tank reaches plane in 360/(9cos37°) = 360/7.2 = 50 s; shell flight T = 2(100 sin53°)/10 = 16 s → fire at 50 − 16 = 34 s
